name: Ginger
aliases: ginger, ground ginger, ginger powder, ginger extract, ginger flavouring, ginger root, Zingiber officinale, jengibre, gingembre, Ingwer, zenzero, gengibre
what_is: Ginger is the root of a plant. It is used fresh, dried or ground, and appears in infusions, biscuits, soft drinks and ready meals. On a label it may say ginger, ginger extract or ginger flavouring, and it does not say how much.
why_botia: In clinical trials, ginger relieved menstrual pain about as well as mefenamic acid, a common painkiller. In pregnant women with nausea and vomiting, it worked about as well as vitamin B6. Those trials used a specific product and a specific dose; a food label does not tell you how much ginger it contains.
can_1: Detect ginger, ginger extract and ginger flavouring when they are declared on the label.
can_2: Explain what the clinical trials found and show the Woman information layer.
cannot_1: Determine how much ginger a food contains, or whether it matches the dose used in the trials.
cannot_2: Tell anyone whether to take ginger, or replace advice from a doctor or a midwife.

sources.label: RCT: ginger vs vitamin B6 for nausea and vomiting in pregnancy (2014)

title: Ginger
description: Ginger is a root used fresh, dried or ground in drinks and foods. In clinical trials it relieved menstrual pain about as well as mefenamic acid, and eased nausea and vomiting in pregnancy about as well as vitamin B6.
